quran-meta-title-check.description: Quran chapter IDs and Arabic/Persian titles were cross-checked against chapter metadata; replacement display titles reference the existing linked English document metadata. These checks do not verify text, translation or rights.

quran-merits-title-check.description: The Persian item titles, chapter names in Quran metadata and linked English document bodies identify five chapter-virtue topics. The replacement English and Arabic display titles are editorial translations, not a verification of the underlying text, translation or rights. The incorrect English document source metadata is preserved separately.

erfan-mujir-review.description: The live Arabic/Persian Mujir presents the disputed divine names in the same order and prints the missing final letters. The legacy edition may differ in wording; only the evident rotation, truncation and typos were changed.

erfan-tawassul-review.description: The live Tawassul text has one occurrence of قرار in the disputed Persian phrase; the legacy duplicate is a transcription error.

erfan-warith-review.description: The Persian instruction is separate from the recited Arabic, and ابن وليه is translated as son of His wali, not son of God.

quran-basmala-duplication.description: In 17 added chapters the bilingual opening is already a separate row and verse 1 begins with the same opening. Remove that repeated prefix from the verse row only. Edition and redistribution rights are separate questions.

unicode-bom.description: A leading U+FEFF byte-order mark is an encoding signature, not Quran text. The previous exact value remains in the history.

alhassanain-item-title-review.description: The relevant Persian headings and the existing English chapter headings identify the item topics; an editorial title correction does not verify the English translation or permission.

treasures-mixed-document-review.description: The pinned source documents contain Arabic/English material for different subjects. Imported introductions from separate non-tr documents had been mixed into those tr documents; preserve their exact references and detach the seven inconsistent item links.

kumayl-audio-menu-review.description: The current source page separates names in audio menus from the text. The eight isolated person names preceding the imported Kumayl introduction are classified as audio-menu artifacts, not prayer or Persian translation. The current audio list need not reproduce the older list.

tawassul-audio-menu-review.description: The current source page separates audio choices from the narrative. The three isolated names at the beginning are audio-menu artifacts; retained in canonical data and omitted from runtime content.

mujir-audio-menu-review.description: The isolated reciter name before the narrative is an audio-menu artifact; retained in canonical data and omitted from runtime content.

parhizkar-audio-menu-review.description: Parhizkar is identified as a Quran reciter. Sixteen isolated occurrences before Quran/chapter-merit content are audio-menu artifacts; this does not classify every similar name in the corpus.

seventh-ali-ziyarat-review.description: The seventh ziyarat has the two disputed Arabic greetings in the later sequence, not before سيد السادات. The Persian had duplicated their translation early. The extra alef is a transcription error; Persian instructions are separate from Arabic recitation. See also https://research.rafed.net/الدعاء-والزيارة/373-الزيارات/3063-الزيارة-السابعة-لأمير-المؤمنين-عليه-السلام.

friday-afternoon-salawat-review.description: The traditional text contains ورحمة الله after the reference to souls and bodies. The exact same Arabic in r00005 has a complete Persian rendering; the r00007 Persian omits souls/bodies and adds an unmatched singular. Instructions are separate from recitation.

ziyarat-hasan-greeting.description: The complete Hasan visitation has ورحمة الله وبركاته in this greeting.

asharat-greeting.description: Dua al-Asharat contains the standard ورحمة الله وبركاته formula at this location.

abu-hamza-greeting.description: The prayer ends with ورحمة الله وبركاته following reference to the souls and bodies.

shaban-greeting.description: The mid-Shaban visitation has السلام عليك ورحمة الله وبركاته.

birthday-ali-greeting.description: This visitation includes يا من له طوبى وحسن مآب ورحمة الله وبركاته.

common-salawat-greeting.description: The standard salawat phrase ends والسلام عليه وعليهم ورحمة الله وبركاته; the Persian translations also retain mercy and blessings.

treasures-record-splitting.description: Each separated paragraph equals all English translation rows of one unique differently numbered pinned upstream record after whitespace folding (SHA-256 e9bc183509323dd85b0a32c43901ca23eaabe660e68abe37bcb314dcba37e65f). Proposed links have multiple matching Arabic source clauses but are not reviewed translation, alignment or rights decisions.

linebreak-ai-assisted-2026-11-06.description: Pre-edit repository snapshot, not an independent source edition. An AI assistant assessed individual line-break contexts at the user’s request; these occurrence-specific formatting edits are unreviewed and do not verify wording, translation, alignment, or rights.

ashura-duplicate-semicolon-crosscheck.description: An independently published presentation of this Ashura phrase shows one semicolon after لِقِتالِكَ; it is a cross-check for the duplicated punctuation only, not proof of the legacy edition, transcription, translation, or rights. An AI assistant made the formatting change and it remains unreviewed. The preceding repository snapshot is 87d20cff548c376f9d133f0d19e0bb349dbe2591.

linebreak-remaining-user-request-2026-11.description: Repository snapshot identifying the exact pre-edit occurrences, not an independent source edition. At the user’s further request an AI assistant joined the 88 previously retained line breaks and moved explicitly recorded list/section/instruction markers; these editorial decisions remain unreviewed and do not establish wording, translation, alignment or rights.
